cross_market_insights: Every market's AI Overview already states that the Bible has no set, word-for-word wedding vow and splits the reader's need in two: verses to read aloud at the ceremony versus verses to weave into personal vows. Our structure should answer both, in that order, and say the 'no set vow' point plainly and sourced.

Sydney and Melbourne page one is weak (Pinterest, small devotional sites, a venue page with garbled text). Brisbane and London are held by Brides, The Knot and Park 31. The AU cities are winnable with a clean, sourced page.
No top result covers Australian law: the words required under the Marriage Act 1961 (s 45 and s 46) and that a minister of religion uses the church's own form. This is the main gap.
No top result explains translation and copyright (most quote NIV, NKJV or ESV text). A public-domain translation (World English Bible or KJV) with references for others is a quiet trust signal.
Nobody covers readings at a destination or symbolic ceremony (who approves, civil-ceremony limits on religious content, reader logistics).

AU demand: the head term is tiny (20/month); 'bible readings for weddings' (390) and 'christian wedding vows' (170) carry the volume. UK mirrors this at larger scale (1600 and 480). The title already says 'Ceremony Readings', so the page can earn the readings query too.
payload.recommended_angle: The calm, sourced Australian guide: which verses couples actually use, split into verses for your own vows and verses for readings, quoted from a public-domain translation and linked at the reference, plus the part nobody else covers: the legal words you still need in Australia, how a church ceremony handles its own form, and how readings work at a destination or symbolic ceremony where a Wedded Advisor coordinates the celebrant, readers and order of service.
